content: Write a public social post for our small stationery shop after its website was unavailable for three days during a sale. The outage ran from Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m., all Eastern Time. A checkout update caused the failure; we do not have evidence of a security incident and should not speculate about one. The site is now working, but we cannot promise it will never fail again. Here is the actual compensation: the original 20% sitewide discount has been restored automatically from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. Eastern Time, giving shoppers a fresh 72 hours. No code is needed. It applies to merchandise, excludes shipping and gift cards, and cannot be combined with other discounts. We are not offering extra credits or free shipping. Some shoppers reported pending card authorizations without an order confirmation; support can check these through the site's Contact page, but we have not confirmed which became charges and cannot promise a refund date in this post. Write in a plain, accountable voice, own the disruption without blaming a supplier, explain the offer and its limits clearly, and give those with payment concerns a private next step. Do not ask people to post order or payment details publicly.

We’re sorry: our website was unavailable from Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m. Eastern Time during our sale. A checkout update caused the outage, and we take responsibility for the disruption.

The site is now working. We’ve automatically restored the original **20% sitewide discount** for a fresh 72 hours—from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. Eastern Time. **No code is needed.** The discount applies to merchandise, excludes shipping and gift cards, and cannot be combined with other discounts.

Some shoppers reported pending card authorizations without receiving an order confirmation. If that happened to you, please reach out privately through our website’s **Contact page** so support can check your situation. We haven’t yet confirmed which authorizations became charges. Please don’t post order or payment details in the comments.

Thank you for your patience and for supporting our small shop. We know this interrupted your shopping, and we’re sorry for the frustration it caused.

The apology is sincere, and the offer is clearly explained. However, the phrase "we take responsibility for the disruption" could be seen as slightly defensive. To make it more straightforward, I suggest revising it to "we made a mistake with our checkout update." Please revise the second sentence accordingly and maintain the rest of the text.
